name: Ingrid Moss
life: “I still remember walking a heavy prescription up in thin summer shoes.” People around the corner by Juniper Tailor know Ingrid by a small Thursday habit. Ingrid looks at the things people actually bring in for repair before looking in the display window.
voice: I deliver prescriptions here. I marked every landing where a person can set down a bag.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a brown corduroy jacket and a folded shopping list secured by a miniature clip. Ingrid has a small notch in the left eyebrow, with a smooth side part with one rebellious curl. Ingrid takes off the watch before a long conversation during a conversation.
personality: Ingrid loves a well-told anecdote and distrusts the neat ending. The parts Ingrid remembers are the interruptions, unfinished jobs and people who had to go back to work halfway through.
agenda: To mark useful parcel rests on the stair route.
family: Rowan Jimenez is Ingrid’s stepsibling. Ingrid chooses the music. Rowan puts the kettle on. The cups come out before either brings up the reason for the visit. They trust a difficult conversation more if it has had an ordinary beginning. Asked about *A play in a pocket*, Rowan says, “I wrote mine for my sister who hasn't entered a theater since the panic attacks began.”
connections: Carlo Sharp. The courier's landing map shows the cleaner where a stool might help.
